title: Cohomology bounds descend from finite local models
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $\Gamma$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $R=\Gamma(*)$ and $\Gamma_T=p_T^*\Gamma$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] for schemes $T$. Let $Q\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Gamma_S))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $\{V_i\to S\}_{i=1}^n$ is a finite covering family of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site]. Fix integers $r\le s$ and scalar cochain complexes $Q_i^\bullet$ with $Q_i^q=0$ for $q\notin[r,s]$. Assume $Q|_{V_i}\simeq\Gamma_{V_i}\otimes_R Q_i^\bullet$ in the derived category, where scalar modules mean constant sheaves as in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Assume each functor $M\mapsto\Gamma_{V_i}\otimes_R M$ on $R$-modules is exact and every $H^q(Q_i^\bullet)$ is finitely presented over $R$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Then $H^q(Q)=0$ for $q\notin[r,s]$, and
$$H^q(Q)|_{V_i}\simeq\Gamma_{V_i}\otimes_R H^q(Q_i^\bullet).$$
In particular each $H^q(Q)$ has a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] and is constructible on the single stratum $S$, so $Q\in\Dbc(S,\Gamma)$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude].

source.place: (2) Local models, global bounds: exact scalar extension, finite scalar cohomology, and descent by the sheaf axiom

proof.text: For $u_i:V_i\to S$, identify $S_{\mathrm{proét}}/V_i$ with $(V_i)_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Indeed an object $W\to V_i$ weakly étale over $V_i$ is weakly étale over $S$ by composition; conversely a map to $V_i$ from a weakly étale $S$-scheme is weakly étale by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. The arrows agree, and the covering families agree since both sites use the same fpqc covering condition [sk-def-pe-site]. By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], localized inverse image of sheaves is sectionwise restriction. Under the identification just made, the abelian inverse image $u_{i,\mathrm{Ab}}^*$ along $u_i$ is this localized restriction, and the canonical isomorphism $\alpha_{u_i}:u_{i,\mathrm{Ab}}^*\Gamma_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma_{V_i}$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] gives ring isomorphisms $\theta_W:\Gamma_S(W)\cong\Gamma(W,\Gamma_W)$ compatible with restriction along every map $W'\to W$ over $V_i$, and carrying multiplication by a section to multiplication by its image [lem-sfb-coefficient-sections-localization]. Hence $\alpha_{u_i}$ identifies the restricted coefficient ring $\Gamma_S|_{V_i}$ with $\Gamma_{V_i}$. Renaming a module action along this ring isomorphism and along its inverse gives inverse equivalences of module categories. Thus the notation $Q|_{V_i}$ uses the exact localized restriction, with the coefficient ring renamed; at a test object $W\to V_i$, restriction of a module sheaf $F$ has sections $F(W)$.

source.place: Definition big-small-proetale; Stacks Tag 092A (weakly étale stability); sites-modules.tex, Tag 03DH, definition-localize-ringed-site; blueprint coefficient morphisms, final sentence

proof.text:
Restriction on module sheaves is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; the coefficient-ring renaming in Step 1 is an equivalence and hence preserves kernels and cokernels by their universal properties. Choose a complex $K^\bullet$ representing $Q$ in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to restriction: its termwise image represents $Q|_{V_i}$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to that same exact functor gives
$$H^q(Q)|_{V_i}\cong H^q(Q|_{V_i}).$$
The two cohomology objects here are those of the representing complexes, since the cohomology functor on the derived category factors the complex cohomology functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, combined with homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, and localized-module exactness (sites-modules.tex Tag 03DH)

proof.text:
Put $E_i(M)=\Gamma_{V_i}\otimes_{R_{V_i}}M_{V_i}$, where $R_{V_i}$ and $M_{V_i}$ are the constant sheaves specified in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. This is the functor assumed exact in the item. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to $E_i:R\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}\to\operatorname{Mod}(\Gamma_{V_i})$ and the scalar complex $Q_i^\bullet$. It yields $H^q(E_i(Q_i^\bullet))\cong E_i(H^q(Q_i^\bullet))$. The given derived isomorphism $Q|_{V_i}\simeq E_i(Q_i^\bullet)$ induces an isomorphism on cohomology by functoriality [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Combining with Step 2 proves, for every $i,q$,
$$H^q(Q)|_{V_i}\cong\Gamma_{V_i}\otimes_R H^q(Q_i^\bullet).$$
Exactness is used only for the scalar extension functor in the hypothesis; no flatness of an arbitrary condensed coefficient ring is asserted.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, applied to the scalar complex; the derived-category functoriality is the definition in the project node def-weil-abstract-derived-category.

proof.text: If $q\notin[r,s]$, the scalar middle term $Q_i^q$ is zero, so $H^q(Q_i^\bullet)=\ker d_i^q/\operatorname{im}d_i^{q-1}=0$ by the definition of complex cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. An exact additive functor sends the zero object to zero. Hence Step 3 gives $H^q(Q)|_{V_i}=0$ for all $i$.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, together with the elementary kernel/image formula for complex cohomology (project node def-weil-abstract-derived-category).

proof.text: Fix $q\notin[r,s]$ and write $F=H^q(Q)$. For every object $W\to S$ of the site, base change of the given covering is a covering $\{W\times_S V_i\to W\}_i$, by the covering axiom of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Step 4 and the sectionwise description [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] give $F(W\times_S V_i)=0$. For any section $x\in F(W)$, its restrictions and those of the zero section are therefore equal on this covering. The equalizer (in particular uniqueness) clause of the sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] implies $x=0$. Thus every section module of $F$ is zero, so $F=0$. This also treats an empty covering: the sheaf axiom then makes $F(W)$ a singleton.

source.place: Tags 00VH and 00VM, definition-site (base change axiom) and definition-sheaf-sets (equalizer and uniqueness)

proof.text: For any $q$, the given modules $H^q(Q_i^\bullet)$ are finitely presented over $R$. The isomorphisms of Step 3 and the given pro-étale covering therefore satisfy exactly the definition of a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. The single immersion $\operatorname{id}_S:S\to S$ gives a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification]: its sole image is all of $S$, which is locally closed and constructible. Explicitly, $S$ and $\varnothing$ are open and retrocompact, so $S=S\cap(S\setminus\varnothing)$ is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Thus $H^q(Q)$ is constructible on that stratum by clause (1) of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. For the affine-local convention on a non-qcqs scheme, use the equivalent scalar-matrix cokernel presentations in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Restrict them to the base-changed cover of an affine open: exact restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] preserves these cokernels and finite direct sums, and the entries remain the same scalar entries under the canonical coefficient restrictions of Step 1, since multiplication by a section restricts to multiplication by its restriction [lem-sfb-coefficient-sections-localization]. The same finite scalar presentations then give finite constant local models on the affine open. Step 5 confines cohomology to the finite integer interval $[r,s]$. Clause (2) of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] now gives $Q\in\Dbc(S,\Gamma)$.

source.place: Tag 03DH, restriction of module sheaves, combined with the finite-presentation and constructibility definitions recorded by the cited project nodes; the one-stratum and affine-local assembly is written out by the agent.
